title: Unveiling Social Media Comments with a Novel Named Entity Recognition System for Identity Groups
benchmark_measurement: The ability of a Named Entity Recognition (NER) model to identify and tag text spans containing attacks against religious identity groups. The performance was measured using precision, recall, and F1-Score.
models_tested: Custom transformer-based Named Entity Recognition (NER) model
findings: The developed NER model performed solidly in identifying attacks on religious groups, achieving an F1-score of 0.72. This 'Religion' category was the most represented in the dataset with 41,002 entities in total. The case study found 80 comments mentioning religion, with some news articles triggering inter-category attacks involving religion and other identities (e.g., gender, sexual orientation). There was a negligible correlation between mentions of religious groups and user engagement metrics like comments, shares, or reactions.
